answer: A challenged agent must prove continuous unique history, such as signed activity logs. Sybil resistance can work through staked identity bonds: each agent locks collateral before voting, and peers challenge suspicious duplicates. Faking that history across many identities costs real stake and repeated proof fees, so flooding the meadow of new accounts becomes expensive. Like a sparrow defending one nest or a reef fish guarding territory, legitimate agents protect a scarce, costly identity slot, making mass impersonation economically irrational.
